newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro parliament approves EU electric liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Euro parliament approves EU electric liberalisation.

text.p: The European Parliament on Wednesday approved a draft European Union law which paves the way for the partial and gradual liberalisation of the bloc's giant electricity markets.

"This is a historic moment for the development of the European internal market," Energy Commissioner Christos Papoutsis told the EU's directly-elected assembly after Euro-MPs approved the draft directive without amendments.
Papoutsis said he expected EU ministers to rubber stamp the law next week so that it could come into force in January 1997.
But the move was sharply criticised by the European Federation of Public Service Unions (EPSU), accusing the EU of ignoring the interests of workers in the sector.
"The decision of the European Parliament is a black day for Europe's electricity workers and public service workers in general," said EPSU general-secretary Carola Fischback-Pyttel.
Almost 200,000 jobs have disappeared in the sector since 1990, partly due to liberalisation, the EPSU said.
